info.description: Human sessions that prove a second factor carry auth_time: the original sign-in time, preserved across refresh. Refresh changes iat but never reopens the sudo window. Machine credentials never carry this proof. Sensitive actions require 2FA; administrative/read/sending grants, credential creation, password/2FA changes and audit access additionally require proof within 15 minutes. FRESH_TWO_FACTOR_WINDOW may shorten that window; invalid, non-positive or longer values refuse startup. Missing or stale proof returns 403 recent_two_factor_required so clients can sign in again. Initial authenticator enrollment and forced password setup before any factor exists remain available; once a factor is enrolled, sign in with it before changing the password.

post.summary: Make a scoped OAuth client secret
post.description: Requires a human session signed in with a second factor, the current password, and mailbox:manage on the account. Returns client_id and client_secret once; stores only the secret hash. Permissions must be within both the creator's and the account's live grants. The client-secret tier accepts mail:read, mail:write, mail:send and mail:receive; domains:read, accounts:read and pipelines:read/write/delete require a domain scope. It rejects all other capabilities, including account/credential creation, granting, password/2FA, audit, retention and server-ceiling controls. expires_at defaults to 90 days. Credential creation is audited as client_secrets.create with actor and credential id. Client secrets exchange at /api/v1/oauth/token; they are never accepted as bearer API keys or mail-client passwords.

put.summary: Set the account's contact reply-time setting
put.description: Opt in to contact reply-time estimates in contact lists and suggestions. Uses the median of at least three first replies matched by In-Reply-To, or the last References ID when In-Reply-To is absent, to this account's Sent messages addressed to the contact. Uses stored received_at timestamps, ignores drafts, deleted mail and nonpositive delays, and counts each sent Message-ID once. This is a local estimate, not a signal from the contact. No headers, outbound requests or tracking are added.

post.summary: Store a message the account already has
post.description: Stores original message octets, folder, supported system flags and required internal_date without delivery rules or push notifications. Requires mail:import on the destination, which every account holds on its own mailbox. A message whose Message-ID and exact octets are already in that account and folder is skipped without changing its flags or date; the same Message-ID with different octets is stored as another message. Messages without Message-ID use a deterministic SHA-256 import identity; the raw source remains unchanged. Every attempt is audited; successful imports and skips also receive a transactional messages.import audit entry. The decoded message is bounded by SMTP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (10 MiB by default); the general API body limit may be stricter. Deleted-state and keyword flags are unsupported and refused rather than hidden or discarded.

After the signing switch, the previous key is retained until retire_after, then revoked with an empty p=. revoked_at records when the worker requested revocation. revocation_published_at records when that record first resolved; removes_after is one TTL later, when it can be removed. These optional fields appear as each step completes. State remains retiring until removal.

delete.description: A domain containing accounts or aliases is refused with 409 domain_not_empty. An empty domain and its live pipelines, custom filters, sender rules, certificates, rotation keys, MTA-STS policy, relay credentials and suppressions are removed atomically. Grants on the domain and its mailbox scopes, including eligible activations, are removed through the audited grant-change mechanism; cached permissions are invalidated only after commit. Historical TLS reports, message traces, aggregate reports and audit entries are retained under their original identities and existing retention rules. A cleanup, audit or cancellation failure rolls the deletion back.

post.summary: Exchange a client secret for a five-minute access token
post.description: RFC 6749 client_credentials grant. Send grant_type=client_credentials and authenticate with the credential's public client_id and client_secret, either in this form or with HTTP Basic (never both). Returns a 300-second bearer access token, without a refresh token or human two-factor authentication. Permissions are selected at credential creation; a scope request is refused. Every use reloads the credential and live account grants, so revocation, expiry, account disablement and removed grants take effect on the next request. Shares the sign-in throttle. Successful issue is audited as oauth.token_issue with the actor and credential id. Responses are Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache.

post.summary: Deliver a message via RESTMAIL protocol
post.description: Server-to-server delivery. Unauthenticated at the HTTP layer: a delivery must come from a trusted peer network or carry a DKIM signature aligned with its From domain, or it is refused 403 unauthorized. The inbound pipeline can refuse it 403 rejected or defer it 503 deferred. When no recipient takes the message the answer is 422 undeliverable. Failed sender/recipient or inbound-policy lookups and corrupt stored policy defer with 503; recipient lookups finish before delivery side effects.
